newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest-July 29.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest-July 29.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

BONN - Telecommunications group Deutsche Telekom declares an advertising victory at the Tour de France where the team it sponsored not only won the race but invaluable worldwide publicity. Telekom spokesman Ulrich Lissek says the company's brand-name recognition has reached about 96 percent in Germany through its sponsorship of the cyclists. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Advertising income at private German television stations has a solid potential for growth through the year 2000, bank analysts say. Ad income at private channels could increase five percent every year until the end of the millennium, analysts from the DG Bank say in a report, which would mean a 27 percent expansion of industry turnover from 1995. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Tag Heuer, Swiss manufacturer of luxury sport watches, says it has signed a contract with tennis star Boris Becker naming him "representative and ambassador of the brand-name". (Horizont)

FRANKFURT - Ad agency Wilkens in Hamburg has won the Kimberly-Clark account and will represent the company's Kleenex, Scott/Scottex and Servus lines. The account is said to be in the tens of millions-mark range. (Horizont)

FRANKFURT - Hygiene- and household-products manufacturer Reckitt & Colman will continue to work with agency McCann-Erickson on its European-wide ad account. Until now, McCann-Erickson and Euro RSCG shared the account, which is worth an estimated $330 million. (Horizont)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
LONDON - NTT, the $160 billion Japanese telecoms titan, says it is focusing European investment plans on second carriers in the key markets of France and Germany. (Reuter)

COLOGNE - Private television station RTL says it strengthened its lead in the German market in the first half of the year. With gross advertising income reaching 1.75 billion marks ($952.9 million), RTL says it achieved a market share of more than 30 percent according to data provided by market research company Nielsen. (Reuter)

KRONBERG - RTL chief executive Helmut Thoma renews his call for more flexible advertising rules. He argues in Tele Images magazine that a less-regulated TV market would finance more diverse programming. Thoma says he supports greater flexibility and not necessarily an increase in the amount of advertising on TV. (Reuter)
WALLDORF - Hiel/BBDO of Munich is the new ad agency for women's programming station TM3. Springer & Jacoby was the station's previous account holder. (Kress)
FRANKFURT - For many manufacturers and retailers catalogues comprise a key part of their traditional advertising. (Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

MUNICH - Luxury carmaker BMW says group net profit surged 30 percent to 435 million marks in the first half of 1997. Sales rose 15.5 percent increase to 29.10 billion marks and group deliveries rose eight percent to 601,070 units. (Reuter)

BONN - The annual summer sales in the German retail sector began promisingly in good weather, the German retail association (HDE) says. HDE spokesman Thomas Werz says hundreds of bargain hunters lined up on pavements in front of major department stores in Munich, Berlin and Hanover ahead of the start of the sales. (Reuter)

BUDAPEST - Volkswagen AG continues to widen its lead in central Europe's booming market for new autos in May, while Daewoo Group overtakes Fiat SPA for second place, according to a monthly Reuters survey. (Reuter)

WIESBADEN - Germany's trade surplus in May falls 5.7 percent to 9.8 billion marks, down from 10.4 billion marks the previous month, according to preliminary data from the Federal Statistics Office. (Reuter)
